note: Formal cores: one mathematical structure, many field bindings. Draft seed written from general knowledge without reading bench answer files. Every entry is draft and unverified against sources. assumptions_met codes: y = normally met, ~ = met approximately, n = normally violated, ? = not known.

cores.name: Recursive linear-Gaussian state estimation
cores.structure: A hidden state evolves linearly with Gaussian noise and is observed linearly with Gaussian noise; the posterior stays Gaussian and is updated recursively.

roles.dynamics: rule that moves the state forward
roles.observation: measured quantity and its relation to the state
roles.gain: weight given to the new measurement

assumptions.text: Dynamics and observation are linear in the state.
Noises are zero-mean, white and Gaussian with known covariances.
The model is correct: no unmodelled bias or drift.
The state is detectable from the observations.

cores.guarantee: The estimate is the minimum-variance unbiased estimate of the state given all past observations.

bindings.tool: Kalman filter for navigation and tracking
breaks: Sensor bias and outliers violate the noise model.
Nonlinear plants need the extended or unscented variants, which lose the optimality guarantee.

bindings.tool: Data assimilation in weather and ocean forecasting

roles.state: atmospheric or ocean fields on a grid

breaks: The dynamics are strongly nonlinear.
The state is too large to hold a full covariance, so ensembles approximate it.

roles.gain: filter weight on the data surprise

breaks: The model itself is contested, so a3 is the weak point.
Agents react to the estimate, which changes the dynamics.

roles.state: property of the world being perceived

breaks: The nervous system's internal noise model cannot be read directly.
Reported departures from optimal weighting are part of the evidence, not noise.

cores.name: Diffusion (parabolic transport)
cores.structure: A conserved density spreads with flux proportional to its gradient; equivalently, the density of many independent small random steps.

assumptions.text: Flux is proportional to the gradient of the density.
The underlying steps are many, independent and of finite variance.
Diffusivity is constant or varies smoothly and does not depend on the density.
The quantity is conserved in the interior.

cores.guarantee: Solutions smooth out, obey a maximum principle and spread in proportion to the square root of time.

breaks: Signals propagate at infinite speed in the model.
Fails far from equilibrium and at scales near the mean free path.
Properties vary with temperature in real materials.
Phase change adds a moving boundary.

bindings.tool: Option pricing by the Black–Scholes equation

roles.density: option value as a function of price and time

breaks: Returns have heavy tails and jumps, which violates a2.
Volatility changes over time and with price.
Hedging is neither continuous nor free.

roles.density: probability density of an allele frequency
roles.boundary: loss or fixation of the allele

breaks: Diffusivity depends on the frequency itself and vanishes at the boundaries.
Small populations are not well approximated.

roles.boundary: pure noise at the final step

breaks: Generation runs the process backwards, which needs a learned score function.
The guarantee covers the forward process only.
The accumulated evidence is inferred from response times, not observed.
Fit quality depends on added parameters.

cores.name: Convergence of a Markov chain to its stationary distribution
cores.structure: A memoryless random process on a set of states settles to one long-run distribution, whatever its starting point.

roles.stationary: long-run share of time in each state

assumptions.text: The next state depends only on the current state.
Every state can be reached from every other state.
The chain is aperiodic.
Transition probabilities do not change over time.

cores.guarantee: A unique stationary distribution exists and the chain converges to it from any start.

bindings.tool: Monte Carlo sampling of equilibrium ensembles
breaks: Near phase transitions the chain mixes very slowly.
Energy barriers can make a2 fail in practice.

roles.kernel: follow a random link or jump at random

breaks: The random jump is added to force a2 and a3.
Real readers are not memoryless.

roles.states: nucleotides or amino acids at a site

breaks: Rates vary across sites and lineages.
Sites are not independent of one another.
Higher-order reactions make the kernel depend on concentrations.
Rate constants change with temperature.
Citation practice differs between fields and changes over time.
The score measures attention, not quality.

cores.name: Convex optimisation and its dual
cores.structure: A convex problem has a paired dual problem; under a constraint qualification both have the same value, and dual variables price the constraints.

roles.dual: marginal value of relaxing each constraint

assumptions.text: The objective and the feasible set are convex.
A constraint qualification holds (for example a strictly feasible point exists).
The problem data are known.

cores.guarantee: Primal and dual optima are equal, and each dual variable equals the marginal value of its constraint.

bindings.tool: Shadow prices and competitive equilibrium prices
breaks: Increasing returns and indivisible goods break convexity.
Externalities mean prices no longer equal marginal social value.
Convexity fails inside phase-coexistence regions.
Small systems and long-range forces can make the potentials non-equivalent.
Deep networks are not convex, so the duality guarantee is lost.
It holds for linear and kernel models.
Assumes perfectly plastic material and small displacements.
Buckling and brittle fracture fall outside the theory.

cores.name: Fourier analysis of shift-invariant linear systems
cores.structure: Complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of every linear shift-invariant operator, so convolution becomes multiplication in the frequency domain.

assumptions.text: The system is linear.
The system is invariant under shifts in time or space.
The signal has finite energy, or is sampled above twice its highest frequency.

cores.guarantee: The system acts on each frequency independently, and energy is preserved between the two domains.

roles.spectrum: amplitude and phase at each frequency

breaks: Saturation and switching devices are nonlinear.
Component values drift, which breaks strict time invariance.

roles.signal: field amplitude in space and time
roles.system: wave equation in a uniform medium

breaks: Non-uniform media couple the modes.
Large amplitudes bring nonlinear effects.
Finite acquisition time limits resolution.
Detector nonlinearity distorts strong signals.

roles.signal: electron density in the unit cell
roles.basis: plane waves indexed by reciprocal-lattice vectors

breaks: Only magnitudes are measured, so the phases are lost.
Disorder and multiple scattering break the simple transform.

roles.basis: sinusoids or normal modes of the Earth
roles.system: Earth response between source and station

breaks: The Earth is laterally varied, so the response is not shift-invariant in space.
Strong ground motion is nonlinear near the source.

cores.name: Replicator dynamics
cores.structure: The share of each type grows at a rate equal to its fitness minus the population's mean fitness.

roles.fitness: growth rate of a type given the current shares

assumptions.text: The population is large and well mixed.
Fitness depends only on the current shares.
No new types appear by mutation or innovation.
Change is continuous in time.

cores.guarantee: Shares rise for types fitter than average, and stable rest points correspond to evolutionarily stable states.

breaks: Mutation and recombination create new types.
Small populations drift.
Spatial structure changes the outcome.

roles.fitness: per-capita growth given the other species

breaks: The mapping needs interaction terms that are linear in abundance.
Total abundance is an extra variable with no counterpart.

bindings.tool: Imitation and learning dynamics in games
breaks: People innovate and look ahead.
Payoffs are not copied with reliable fidelity.
Copying errors produce a mutant cloud.
Constant total concentration must be enforced by the reactor.
Updates are discrete steps.
Rewards may be set by an adversary, not by the weights.

cores.name: Maximum-entropy inference
cores.structure: Among all distributions that match stated averages, the one with greatest entropy has exponential-family form.

assumptions.text: The stated constraints are the only relevant information.
The state space and its base measure are well defined.
The constrained averages are known accurately.

cores.guarantee: The maximiser is unique and is an exponential family with one multiplier per constraint.

breaks: Applies at equilibrium only.
Systems that do not explore their state space violate it.

roles.constraints: feature averages matched to the data

breaks: Feature choice decides what counts as information.
Finite samples make the constrained averages noisy.

roles.states: assignments of trips to origin–destination pairs
roles.constraints: trip totals and total travel cost

breaks: Travellers are not interchangeable particles.
The model describes a pattern and does not explain choices.

roles.states: allocations of individuals and energy to species
roles.constraints: totals of species, individuals and metabolic rate

breaks: Contested: disturbed communities depart from the predictions.
It gives patterns with no mechanism.

cores.name: Linear flow on a network (graph Laplacian)
cores.structure: Flow on each edge is proportional to a potential difference and is conserved at nodes; potentials solve a Laplacian system.

roles.weights: ease of flow on each edge

assumptions.text: Flow on an edge is linear in the potential difference.
Flow is conserved at every interior node.
Edge weights are symmetric.
The network is connected.

cores.guarantee: Potentials are unique given boundary values, and effective resistance between nodes is proportional to random-walk commute time.

breaks: Diodes and transistors are nonlinear and one-way.
High frequencies need distributed models.
Turbulent head loss grows roughly with the square of flow.
The network must be solved by iteration.
The similarity graph is a modelling choice.
Directed relations do not fit symmetric weights.

roles.potential: probability of reaching a target patch

breaks: Animals do not move as memoryless random walkers.
Movement is often easier one way than the other.
The shared structure is the adjacency spectrum, not conserved flow.
Electron repulsion is ignored.

cores.name: Stability by a Lyapunov function
cores.structure: If an energy-like function is positive away from an equilibrium and never increases along trajectories, the equilibrium is stable.

assumptions.text: A function exists that is positive away from the equilibrium and zero at it.
The function does not increase along any trajectory.
The dynamics are well posed (locally Lipschitz).
The model matches the real system.

cores.guarantee: The equilibrium is stable, and asymptotically stable when the function strictly decreases.

breaks: Actuator saturation and delay are often left out of the model.
The proof covers the model, not the hardware.
Holds near equilibrium.
Driven systems need not have such a function.
Real communities are noisy, seasonal and spatial.
The function is known only for special interaction structures.

roles.function: loss or distance to the minimiser

breaks: Stochastic gradients make the function decrease only on average.
Non-convex losses have many rest points.
Stability needs strong conditions on demand, such as gross substitutes.
No real market follows the assumed adjustment rule.

cores.name: Variational principle and optimal control
cores.structure: A path that makes an integral stationary satisfies local differential conditions, with a costate variable conjugate to the state.

roles.path: state as a function of time

assumptions.text: Dynamics and cost are smooth.
End conditions are specified.
The system is deterministic.
Enough convexity holds for the stationary path to be a minimum.

cores.guarantee: The optimal path satisfies the Euler–Lagrange or Pontryagin conditions, and each continuous symmetry gives a conserved quantity.

breaks: The action is stationary, not always minimal.
Friction needs an extended formulation.

roles.running_cost: quadratic penalty on error and effort

breaks: Actuator limits make the true problem constrained.
Disturbances make the system stochastic.
A single planner with known preferences is assumed.
The horizon is infinite, so the end condition is a limit.

roles.path: body size or reserves over the lifetime
roles.control: share of energy given to growth or reproduction
roles.costate: reproductive value of a unit of size

breaks: No agent performs the optimisation; selection only approximates it.
Survival is random and environments vary.

cores.name: Branching-process threshold
cores.structure: Each individual independently leaves a random number of successors; the line dies out with certainty unless the mean number exceeds one.

assumptions.text: Units reproduce independently of one another.
All units share one offspring distribution.
Nothing limits growth in the phase considered.

cores.guarantee: Extinction is certain when the mean is at most one; above one, survival has positive probability and growth is exponential.

breaks: Infectiousness varies widely between people.
Susceptibles run out, so a3 holds only early.
Contact networks are clustered.

roles.offspring: neutrons from the fission one neutron causes

breaks: Delayed neutrons and temperature feedback change the multiplication factor over time.
Geometry makes neutrons non-identical.

bindings.tool: Survival probability of a new beneficial mutation

roles.offspring: copies left in the next generation

breaks: Valid while the mutant is rare.
Linked selection breaks independence.
Adoption often needs several exposures, which breaks independence.
Influence is very unequal across people.

cores.name: Bayesian updating
cores.structure: Belief in each hypothesis after evidence is proportional to prior belief times the probability of the evidence under that hypothesis.

roles.likelihood: probability of the evidence under each hypothesis

assumptions.text: The hypotheses are mutually exclusive and exhaustive.
The likelihood model is correct.
The prior is stated.
Items of evidence multiplied together are conditionally independent.

cores.guarantee: The posterior is the unique coherent revision of the prior given the evidence.

bindings.tool: Predictive value of a diagnostic test
breaks: Sensitivity and specificity shift with the patient population.
Repeated tests are rarely independent.

bindings.tool: Bayesian age modelling and radiocarbon calibration

roles.likelihood: measured isotope ratio given the calibration curve

breaks: The calibration curve carries its own uncertainty.
Reworked or contaminated samples violate the likelihood model.

roles.likelihood: probability of the sequences given a tree

breaks: Substitution models are simplified.
Priors on trees can dominate weak data.

bindings.tool: Structured probabilistic judgement in intelligence analysis

roles.hypotheses: competing explanations of an adversary's behaviour
roles.likelihood: how expected each report is under each explanation

breaks: The true explanation may not be on the list.
An adversary may plant evidence, so the likelihood model is itself contested.
Reports often share one source.

roles.likelihood: probability of the forensic finding under each proposition

breaks: Contested: courts differ on whether numbers may be put to a jury.
The standard of proof is a legal warrant, not a probability threshold.
